steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Rivetbay on this bench turns event descriptions into field decoders. Descriptions live at `/app/rivetbay/evd/*.evd`. One mill pass must refresh `/app/rivetbay/intake/current.ledger` from those files and write one `/app/rivetbay/emitters/<name>.kdec` per description discovered on that run. `/app/bin/rivetbay mill` is that pass; `/app/bin/rivetbay decode <frame>` prints JSON for a sample under `/app/rivetbay/frames`. A description with no decoder decodes as unknown.

Some descriptions on disk currently finish mill without a matching `.kdec`, decode as unknown, and leave emitters short of the on-disk descriptions; mill must exit non-zero when decoders are fewer than descriptions. One mill subprocess must leave emitters equal to the descriptions present for that run, and decode of a newly added event must print its fields.

Update the C code in the mill pipeline under `/app/rivetbay` so each pass regenerates the ledger and `.kdec` files from descriptions on disk, then rebuild `/app/bin/rivetbay`. Hand-written ledger or decoder files are not enough. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/rivetbay mill` and `/app/bin/rivetbay decode` on fresh descriptions and frames. Ledger lines are `name|relpath|field:kind,...` with kinds `u8` and `u16` in description order; mill must keep prior ledger row order and append newly discovered descriptions after existing rows. Each `.kdec` starts with `KDEC1`, then `NAME <name>`, then one `field kind` line per field. Decode JSON is `{"kind":"decoded","name":"<name>","fields":{...}}` with integer field keys from the description (such as mm, latch, force, amp, bit, thick, q, n, and w), or `{"kind":"unknown","name":"<name>"}` when no decoder exists. Frame bytes are a 4-byte big-endian name length, the name, then packed big-endian field payloads.

Current Terminal Screen:

Analysis: We are at a root shell in /app with no prior investigation shown. The C mill pipeline must be inspected to identify why some descriptions do not produce ledger rows and decoder files, then rebuilt and tested.
Plan: Inspect the project layout, source files, build configuration, current descriptions, ledger, emitters, and CLI behavior. This will establish the description format and locate the mill implementation before making changes.

steps.message:
Analysis: There are eight descriptions but only seven ledger rows and emitters; galley_hatch is omitted. The visible emitter code is artificially capped by sheet_emit_cap(), which likely explains missing decoders. The mill must also remove stale emitters, preserve prior ledger ordering, append newly discovered descriptions, regenerate rows from current EVD contents, and return non-zero if counts diverge. More source details were truncated, especially discovery, snapshot/sheet, driver, and millscore integration.
Plan: Inspect all pipeline source files and external millscore code individually without truncation, plus notes and the current mill/decode exit behavior. Then replace or correct the faulty discovery/snapshot/emission logic at its source rather than hand-editing generated files.

arguments.keystrokes: cd /app/rivetbay; for f in forgekit/discover.c forgekit/discover.h forgekit/snapshot.c forgekit/sheet.h forgekit/driver.c forgekit/warmup.c forgekit/warmup.h; do echo "===== $f ====="; nl -ba "$f"; done

echo '===== millscore ====='; find /app/millscore -maxdepth 2 -type f -print -exec sh -c 'echo "--- $1"; nl -ba "$1"' sh {} \; 2>/dev/null; echo '===== notes ====='; for f in /app/rivetbay/notes/*; do echo "--- $f"; cat "$f"; done

cd /app/rivetbay; /app/bin/rivetbay mill; rc=$?; echo "mill_rc=$rc"; echo 'ledger:'; cat intake/current.ledger; echo 'emitter count / description count:'; find emitters -maxdepth 1 -name '*.kdec' | wc -l; find evd -maxdepth 1 -name '*.evd' | wc -l; echo 'galley decode:'; /app/bin/rivetbay decode frames/galley_hatch.bin; echo "decode_rc=$?"

steps.message:
Analysis: The failure is confirmed: mill discovers galley_hatch and appends it to the ledger, but snapshot.c retains the pre-discovery line count in g_emit_cap, so emit_all stops after seven rows. Mill then incorrectly returns zero because tally compares emitters against the stale sheet view/cap state. Beyond that immediate bug, emit_all does not remove stale .kdec files, and discover_all reconstructs prior rows by assuming each event name maps to <name>.evd rather than retaining actual discovered relative paths. The implementation needs robust per-run reconciliation.
Plan: Inspect the omitted portion of snapshot.c and current headers, then rewrite discovery and emission as needed: discover every valid .evd, preserve existing ledger name order for descriptions still present, append new descriptions deterministically, regenerate rows from current files, reload the post-discovery ledger for emission, remove stale .kdec files, emit every current row, and ensure mill returns non-zero on any count mismatch. Then rebuild and run baseline plus add/remove/change tests.

arguments.keystrokes: cd /app/rivetbay; echo '===== complete snapshot.c ====='; cat forgekit/snapshot.c; echo '===== parse/emit headers ====='; cat forgekit/parse_evd.h forgekit/emit.h forgekit/sheet.h; echo '===== Makefile visible whitespace ====='; sed -n l Makefile

steps.message:
Analysis: The precise stale-snapshot bug is now fully visible: prime_intake_sheet records both the old ledger and its old line count; discover_all rewrites the ledger, but pour_sheet still processes g_primed. Fixing only the cap would still emit the old ledger. The pipeline must reload the ledger after discovery. Discovery should also preserve prior order by event NAME while using each currently discovered file's actual relative path, and emission should clear stale decoders before regenerating all current ones.
Plan: Rewrite discover.c to collect current valid descriptions, preserve surviving names in prior ledger order, and append new files in deterministic filename order. Rewrite emit.c to remove all old .kdec files and emit every ledger row without a stale cap. Adjust driver.c to reload the newly generated ledger before pour_sheet. Rebuild, then test galley_hatch, ledger/emitter equality, idempotence, changed fields, a newly added event whose filename differs from its NAME, and stale-emitter removal.

steps.message:
Analysis: Baseline succeeded only because the ledger already contained galley_hatch before the rebuilt mill ran. The fresh-description test exposed that driver.c was not actually modified: the string replacement did not match its indentation, so grab_sheet() was never inserted. Consequently emission still used the pre-discovery snapshot, verifier_new remained unknown, and after restoring files one stale verifier decoder was generated from the prior snapshot. Stale-file cleanup itself worked, as stale.kdec was removed.
Plan: Inspect and patch driver.c structurally to call grab_sheet() immediately after discover_all(), rebuild, and rerun mill on the restored eight-description state. Then repeat a clean fresh-description test, verify decoder generation and JSON fields, remove the test description, rerun mill, and confirm the test decoder is removed and final counts match.

steps.message:
Analysis: The mill pipeline has been fixed and rebuilt. It now reloads the regenerated ledger before emission, preserves prior ledger row order, appends newly discovered descriptions, supports description filenames that differ from event names, clears stale decoders, and emits one decoder per current ledger row. Tests confirmed the original galley_hatch event decodes correctly, a newly added verifier event generated a matching decoder and decoded big-endian u16/u8 fields correctly, removed descriptions lose their stale decoders, repeated mill passes preserve ordering, and final description/ledger/emitter counts are all 8.
Plan: No further commands are needed. The source changes are compiled into /app/bin/rivetbay and the project is restored to its original eight-description dataset with regenerated ledger and emitters.
